html:
SMTO-CFG-0048 — SMTO can't start because a database row limit is below zero

GUID: 52e6fc54-47c5-4c03-bee6-8aae4d004753
Slug: config-sql-row-limit-must-be-zero-or
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while starting because a setting that limits how many database rows it returns is a negative number. Your conversations and settings were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the config.yaml file in the SMTO folder, or the file named after --config in the command that starts SMTO, and find the row_limit: line under sql:. SMTO reads this row limit from config.yaml when it starts.
  2. Set row_limit: to 0 to use SMTO's standard limit of 100 rows, or to the positive number of rows you want. Zero tells SMTO to use its standard limit, but a negative number of rows has no meaning.
  3. Save the file, then select Start again on the startup screen, or start SMTO the way you normally do. The corrected limit is used from the next start.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't send config.yaml itself, because it can contain your Model access key. Leave SMTO's other database limits as they are.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Configuration validation rejected sql.row_limit (config.yaml sql.row_limit, checked by SQLConfig.validate_sql and Settings.validate_default_node) because it is negative; zero and positive values are accepted.

What this means

  • SQL compatibility configuration sets row_limit below zero. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • SQL compatibility configuration sets row_limit below zero.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect sql.row_limit and its own zero semantics, separately from native database default/max row controls.

How to fix it

  • Set sql.row_limit in the bootstrap config.yaml (or the file named by AOR_APP_CONFIG_PATH or --config) to 0 or a positive integer and restart the Server; 0 makes the execution engine use its default max_rows_returned of 100. This limit is independent of database_default_limit and database_max_rows.
  • Set sql.row_limit to a supported nonnegative count.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended nonnegative compatibility row limit validates.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
